title: One-Pot Ham, Pea & Cheddar Pasta
description: Pasta, diced ham, peas, and cheddar come together in one pot for a simple comfort meal that is especially handy for leftover ham.
substitutions: Use cooked turkey instead of ham.
Use frozen broccoli instead of peas.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Warm the ham and peas, then finish with cheddar.

cookSteps.text: Put 8 ounces short pasta and 2 1/2 cups chicken broth in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a lively simmer.
Cook 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is nearly tender and only a little liquid remains.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups diced cooked ham and 1 cup frozen peas. Cover and cook 3–4 minutes, until everything is steaming hot.
Remove from the heat. Stir in 1 cup shredded cheddar and up to 1/4 cup milk if you want it creamier. Season to taste and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days, within the original safe storage window for the ham. Reheat until steaming hot with a splash of milk or water.

title: Turkey, Cucumber & Cheddar Toasties
description: Warm cheddar toast topped with deli turkey and cool cucumber makes a quick lunch with ordinary fridge ingredients.
substitutions: Use deli ham instead of turkey.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.
Use thin apple slices instead of cucumber for a sweet-crisp version.

steps.text: Add turkey and cucumber and serve.

cookSteps.text: Top 4 slices sandwich bread with 4 slices cheddar. Toast until the bread is crisp and the cheese is melted, about 3–5 minutes.
Divide 4 ounces deli turkey and the thin slices from 1/2 cucumber over 2 cheese toasts.
Add 1 tablespoon mayonnaise or yogurt to each sandwich if using, top with the remaining cheese toasts, and serve.

storage: Best assembled fresh. Keep turkey and cucumber refrigerated and make only what you plan to eat so the toast stays crisp.

title: Leftover Roasted Vegetable & Egg Rice Bowl
description: Leftover roasted vegetables, rice, and a fried egg become a fast bowl that rescues odds and ends from the fridge.
substitutions: Use leftover cooked potatoes instead of rice and make a hash.
Use frozen mixed vegetables if you do not have roasted vegetables.
Top with shredded cheddar instead of soy sauce.

steps.text: Heat the rice and leftover vegetables.
Fry the eggs and put one on each bowl.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon oil or butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 cups cold cooked rice and 1 1/2 cups chopped roasted vegetables.
Cook 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until the rice and vegetables are steaming hot. Stir in 1 tablespoon soy sauce if using.
Move the rice mixture to 2 bowls. Add the remaining 1 teaspoon oil or butter to the skillet and crack in 2 eggs.
Cook the eggs 2–3 minutes, or until done the way you like. Put 1 egg on each rice bowl and serve.

storage: Best eaten right away. Use the rice and vegetables within their original safe refrigerated storage windows and reheat them until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Chocolate Banana Oat Cookies
description: One ripe banana turns oats and chocolate chips into a tiny batch of soft cookies with almost no cleanup.
substitutions: Use quick oats for a softer texture.
Use sunflower-seed butter instead of peanut butter.
Use raisins instead of chocolate chips.

steps.text: Mash and mix everything in one bowl.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and line or lightly grease a baking sheet.
Mash 1 very ripe banana in a small bowl. Stir in 3/4 cup oats, 2 tablespoons peanut butter, 2 tablespoons chocolate chips, and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon if using.
Drop 6 small mounds onto the baking sheet and flatten each slightly with the back of a spoon.
Bake 10–12 minutes, until the cookies are set and lightly browned at the edges.

storage: Refrigerate in a covered container up to 3 days. These stay soft rather than crisp.

title: Slow Cooker Lentil, Carrot & Potato Soup
description: Lentils, carrots, and potatoes simmer into an inexpensive hands-off soup made from basic pantry and produce staples.
substitutions: Use sweet potatoes instead of white potatoes.
Add 2 cups chopped cabbage for the last hour.
Use water plus bouillon instead of boxed broth.

steps.text: Put everything in the slow cooker.
Cook until the lentils and vegetables are tender.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 cup rinsed lentils, 1 pound diced potatoes, 3 sliced carrots, 6 cups broth, 1 teaspoon garlic powder if using, and 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning if using into the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 6 hours, until the lentils, potatoes, and carrots are tender.
Stir well, taste, season with salt and pepper as needed, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. The soup thickens as it stands; add broth or water when reheating.
